 By Priyanka Stringer Published on November 17, 2026 Hanover Theater — Reported Venue For Contractions
Google Street View Bert Kreischer’s reported promise to help fund a Framingham baby’s college education has not been confirmed as an opened account. Kierra Murphy told MassLive that she was experiencing contractions during Kreischer’s Worcester comedy show on Saturday, Nov. 14, and stayed through the performance. MassLive reported that Kreischer posted an Instagram video the next morning promising to send the child to college.
 As of Monday, Nov. 16, Murphy said she had emailed Kreischer but had not received a response, MassLive reported. The outlet also said his team had not immediately responded to its request for comment. Its report documented the public pledge and Murphy’s outreach; it did not establish that an education account had been opened or funded.
 What a college account would—and would not—show
 Massachusetts’ U.Fund is one way to save for education, but its basic rules do not verify a particular pledge. MEFA says anyone can open a U.Fund account with any amount, and the beneficiary can be someone the account owner chooses. Separately, the Internal Revenue Service says 529-plan earnings are not subject to federal tax when used for qualified education expenses; contributions are not deductible. Neither program information establishes that Murphy’s son has an account.
 Other performances, different outcomes
 Murphy’s reported contractions also differ from two other reported incidents in which an attendee gave birth during a concert. CBS Boston reported that a Pink fan went into labor during the Aug. 1 concert at Fenway Park and later welcomed a baby boy. TODAY.com reported that an attendee gave birth during Karol G’s Oct. 25 concert in Fresno, California, and that the singer later visited the mother and baby at the hospital. Those separate cases involved births during concerts; they do not establish that Murphy gave birth at Kreischer’s show or that such events are becoming more common.
